title: Projective stability and properness of the affine vector orbit map
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], let $r\geq2$, and let $E$ be an $r$-dimensional $k$-vector space. Put $G=\operatorname{SL}(E)$, whose points over a commutative $k$-algebra $R$ are the determinant-one automorphisms of $E\otimes_kR$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Let $V\ne0$ be finite-dimensional and let $G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ be a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes, that is, a rational representation. Let $Y$ be a projective $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-kun-projective] with a $G$-action and a $G$-equivariant closed immersion $j:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The projective space parametrizes lines, and $L=j^*\mathcal O(1)$ is the dual tautological line with its induced linearization. Write $Y^{ss}(L)$ for the locus where some invariant section in $H^0(Y,L^{\otimes n})$, $n>0$, is nonzero. For $y\in Y(k)$ choose $0\ne v\in V$ spanning $j(y)$, and let $\alpha_v:G\to\mathbf A(V)$ be the orbit morphism $g\mapsto gv$. Here $\mathbf A(V)=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Sym}_k V^\vee)$ is affine vector space [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $y\in Y^{ss}(L)$ has orbit closed in $Y^{ss}(L)$ and scheme-theoretic stabilizer of dimension zero if and only if $\alpha_v$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The stabilizer represents $R\mapsto\{g:g y_R=y_R\}$; dimension means Krull dimension of its underlying topological space. No characteristic, reducedness of $Y$, or smoothness of the stabilizer is assumed.

source.place: Chapter 2, Section 1, Proposition 2.2 (affine-cone criterion) and proof of Theorem 2.1 (valuative and elementary-divisor argument). Local book WANTED; agent reconstruction. Morrison Section 2.2, Proposition 1, printed pp.6--7 cites Theorem 2.1.

proof.text: Choose bases of $E$ and $V$. The group $G=\operatorname{SL}(E)$ is smooth, connected, affine, finite type and reductive by [lem-sfb-special-linear-reductive]. Projectivity makes $Y$ separated and finite type: use [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] and the definition of properness. We may therefore apply orbit geometry both to $Y$ and to affine vector space. Write $P=\operatorname{Sym}(V^\vee)$, $P_m$ for its degree-$m$ part, and $L=j^*\mathcal O(1)$. By [sk-thm-picard-pn], $P_m$ is $H^0(\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V),\mathcal O(m))$. In homogeneous coordinates the section is evaluated by $p(w)$, so its action is $(g\cdot p)(w)=p(g^{-1}w)$; consequently restriction to $Y$, multiplication, and evaluation against a chosen lift of a point are equivariant with the induced linearizations. This also fixes the lines versus quotient and O(1) sign conventions.

source.place: Example 19.19 and Proposition 7.4; projective coordinate conventions; affine-cone assembly reconstructed by NH (agent).

proof.text: Assume first that $y$ is stable. Choose an invariant $s\in H^0(Y,L^n)$, $n>0$, nonzero at $y$. By [lem-sfb-projective-polarization-section-algebra] applied to $\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V)$ and its closed subscheme $Y$, choose $M>0$ large enough that $P_{nM}\to H^0(Y,L^{nM})$ is surjective. Its inverse image $W$ of the invariant line $k s^M$ is finite-dimensional and invariant, with an equivariant surjection $\lambda:W\to k$, defined by restriction $w|_Y=\lambda(w)s^M$. Apply [lem-sfb-haboush-symmetric-power-lift] to obtain $N>0$ and $q\in(\operatorname{Sym}^N W)^G$ with $\operatorname{Sym}^N(\lambda)(q)=1$. Multiplication into $P$ sends $q$ to an invariant homogeneous polynomial $f$ of degree $d=nMN>0$ with $f|_Y=s^{MN}$. Thus $c=f(v)\ne0$. This power-lifting argument uses no exactness of invariants, so works in positive characteristic and for nonreduced $Y$.

source.place: Example 19.19; Haboush input is the cited symmetric-power statement; affine-cone assembly reconstructed by NH (agent).

proof.text: Let $I$ be the homogeneous ideal cutting out $Y$, and put $C=\operatorname{Spec}(P/I)$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}(P/(I,f-c))$. These schemes are $G$-invariant: the restriction maps defining $I$ are equivariant and $f$ is invariant. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-slice-finite-cover], vector-to-line gives a finite locally free surjection $p:T\to Y_f$. Here $Y_f\subset Y^{ss}(L)$, since the restriction of $f$ is an invariant section of positive degree. The orbit $O_y=Gy$ is closed in $Y_f$ by the stability assumption. Also $O_v=Gv\subset T$ and $p(O_v)=O_y$.

source.place: Propositions 7.4--7.6; standard projective homogeneous charts; affine-cone assembly reconstructed by NH (agent).

proof.text: We claim $O_v$ is closed in $T$. Its closure is contained in the closed subset $p^{-1}(O_y)$. For every $w\in p^{-1}(O_y)(k)$, its projective stabilizer is conjugate to $G_y$ and has dimension zero. By [lem-sfb-zero-dimensional-stabilizer-finite-orbit] its $k$-points form a finite set. The vector stabilizer $G_w(k)$ is a subgroup of this finite set, hence by the same lemma $\dim G_w=0$. The dimension formula in [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry] gives $\dim O_w=\dim G$ for every such $w$, including $v$. If $\overline{O_v}\setminus O_v$ were nonempty, this invariant locally closed finite-type subset would have a $k$-point (apply [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] on a nonempty affine open). Its orbit would have strictly smaller dimension by orbit geometry, a contradiction. Thus $O_v$ is closed in $T$, and therefore in $\mathbf A(V)$ since $T$ is closed there.

source.place: Propositions 7.4--7.6 and orbit boundary dimension drop; affine-cone assembly reconstructed by NH (agent).

proof.text: The vector stabilizer has dimension zero by the preceding step. By [lem-sfb-zero-dimensional-stabilizer-finite-orbit], $G\to O_v$ is finite locally free, in particular finite. As $O_v$ with its reduced induced structure is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf A(V)$, its inclusion is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Composition [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] proves that $\alpha_v$ is finite, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres].

source.place: Proposition 7.15; finite orbit torsor followed by closed inclusion; affine-cone assembly reconstructed by NH (agent).

proof.text: Conversely assume $\alpha_v$ proper. It is a morphism between affine schemes, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], and finite by [lem-sfb-affine-proper-finite]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] shows that its image $O_v$ is closed and its fibre over $v$ has finitely many points. Those points are $k$-points by [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing], so $G_v(k)$ is finite. The origin is not in $O_v$, since an invertible linear transformation cannot take $v\ne0$ to zero. Give $O_v$ its reduced closed structure; it is invariant and the orbit map factors through it by [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry].

source.place: Proposition 7.4 and the affine-proper-finite equivalence; affine-cone assembly reconstructed by NH (agent).

proof.text: Write $J\subset P$ for the ideal of this reduced closed orbit and $\mathfrak m_0$ for the origin ideal. Since $0\notin V(J)$ choose $a\in J$ with $a(0)=1$, so $u=1-a\in\mathfrak m_0$ restricts to $1$ on $O_v$. Let $M$ be the inverse image of the constant submodule $k\subset P/J$ under $\mathfrak m_0\to P/J$. It is a rational submodule, and restriction gives an equivariant surjection $M\to k$ taking $u$ to $1$. By [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subrepresentation], choose a finite-dimensional invariant submodule $W\subset M$ containing $u$. Apply [lem-sfb-haboush-symmetric-power-lift] to $W\to k$. Multiplication $\operatorname{Sym}^N W\to P$ sends the resulting invariant element to $F\in\mathfrak m_0^G$ restricting to $1$ on $O_v$. The linear action preserves degree, so every homogeneous component $F_d$ is invariant. Since $F_0=0$ and $F(v)=1$, some $d>0$ has $f:=F_d$ with $c=f(v)\ne0$. Its restriction to $Y$ is an invariant section, proving $y\in Y^{ss}(L)$.

source.place: Proposition 4.7 and Corollary 4.8; separation from the origin by the cited Haboush lift; affine-cone assembly reconstructed by NH (agent).

proof.text: Use this $f,d,c$ to form $T$ and $p:T\to Y_f$ as in step 3. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-slice-finite-cover] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], $p$ is closed. Since $O_v$ is closed in $T$, $O_y=p(O_v)$ is closed in $Y_f$. For $g\in G_y(k)$ write $gv=t(g)v$ with $t(g)\in k^\times$. Invariance and homogeneity give $c=f(gv)=t(g)^d c$, so $t(g)^d=1$. This defines a homomorphism $G_y(k)\to\{t\in k^\times:t^d=1\}$ with kernel $G_v(k)$. The image has at most $d$ elements and the kernel is finite by step 6, so $G_y(k)$ is finite. By [lem-sfb-zero-dimensional-stabilizer-finite-orbit], $\dim G_y=0$ as a scheme; no smoothness of this stabilizer is inferred.

source.place: Propositions 7.11--7.15; projective versus vector stabilizer; affine-cone assembly reconstructed by NH (agent).

proof.text: It remains to check closedness in the whole semistable locus. For any invariant $s\in H^0(Y,L^e)$ with $e>0$, let $b$ be its scalar evaluation on $v^{\otimes e}$. On $O_y$ the section $c^e s^d-b^d f^e$ of $L^{ed}$ vanishes: on a lift $tgv$ its two terms are both $c^e b^d t^{ed}$, using invariance of $s$ and $f$. Therefore its closed zero locus contains the closure $Z=\overline{O_y}$ in $Y$. This assertion can also be checked on affine trivializations using [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing]; orbit $k$-points are dense by that lemma. At any $z\in Z$ where $f(z)=0$ the relation gives $c^e s(z)^d=0$, hence $s(z)=0$ in its residue field. This holds for every positive-degree invariant section, so $Z\setminus Y_f$ is disjoint from $Y^{ss}(L)$. Within $Y_f$, $O_y$ is already closed by step 8. Consequently $Z\cap Y^{ss}(L)=O_y$. Together with semistability and the zero-dimensional stabilizer this proves stability of $y$ and the converse implication.
